full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. These 2 (two) civil petitions for leave to appeal (CP) are from the common judgment and decree dated the 13th day of February, 2014 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.124 of 2010 allowing the same and sending the suit back to the trial Court. 

 4. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 23.02.2010 dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed First Appeal No.124 of 2010 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench by the impugned judgment and decree allowed the appeal, and sent the suit back to the trial Court "to pass a proper judgment on the observation made in the body of the judgment." 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the High Court Division, the two sets of defendants have filed these two cps. 

 7. We have gone through the judgment and decree of the trial Court. It appears that the trial Court dismissed the suit on detailed discussion on the evidence, both oral and documentary. The High Court Division without considering and sifting the evidence adduced in the suit, considering extraneous matters and then on the observation. "Now the question is that when government pay the compensation. No documents has been annexed or exhibited to show government at any point of time paid compensation or compensation assessment role has been published as per law. These questions being related to the decision of the suit and are both questions of law and fact needs to be answered afresh" allowed the appeal and sent the suit back to the trial Court to pass a proper judgment in the manner as stated above. This Court has repeatedly held that the order of remand cannot be made as a matter of course or as a matter of fancy. But in this case, it appears to us that the High Court Division sent the suit to the trial Court just as matter of fancy. Since both the parties adduced evidence and the trial Court dismissed the suit discussing the evidence, it was obligatory upon the High Court Division to discuss and sift the evidence and see whether the trial Court rightly considered and sifted the evidence in dismissing the suit in view of the pleading of the respective party. We have also noticed that the High Court Division did not give any direction upon the parties to adduce further evidence in the suit. It also appears to us that the evidence adduced by the parties are sufficient to decide the question posed by the High Court Division finally and conclusively. Therefore, the High Court Division had no reason to send the suit back to the trial Court. 

 9. The impugned judgment and decree is set aside. The first appeal is sent back to the High Court Division for hearing afresh and for disposal on merit in accordance with law on the evidence already on record. Since we are disposing this petition summarily and sending the appeal back to the High Court Division, the application filed by respondent No.6 in C.P No.1426 of 2014 to transpose it as a co-petitioner does not require any consideration on merit However, if so advised, respondent No.6 may contest the appeal in the High Court Division.
